The map's label for smaller Hindu states around 1279 to 1300, scattered from western and southern India to the islands of Southeast Asia. They sat outside the big named powers of the time.

In peninsular India the Chola Empire had just ended in 1279, and its lands were shared among regional dynasties:

  • the Seuna Yadavas of Devagiri in the western Deccan;
  • the Kakatiyas of Warangal, ruled in these years by the queen Rudrama Devi;
  • the Hoysalas in the south;
  • the Pandyas of Madurai, whose coast Marco Polo described around 1292;
  • the Eastern Gangas of Odisha, builders of the Konark Sun Temple.

Their world ended fast. Between 1308 and 1311 the general Malik Kafur of the Delhi Sultanate raided deep into the south and took huge loot. Most of these dynasties fell within a few decades, and new states such as Vijayanagara rose in their place.
